$comment: Parity policy for the shared VfSelect cases. Plain data: no DSL, no waiver engine. The fourth overlay policy, and the first whose overlay holds controls the component owns: every option of an open listbox is a component control. It starts empty and stays empty. What the Razor adapter cannot represent - a consumer that does not write the emitted value back, a teleport target given as an element, options that change after render - is not an approval: the controlled mode is a declared platform divergence with both halves covered, and the rest is recorded below with where it is covered.

classifications.exact: Must match literally across every target. Structure, canonical classes, native attributes, the listbox's inline position and min-width, visible text, accessible names and states, live state, ownership, relationships, focus, the value log, the form entries and the transitions.
classifications.semantic: Framework mechanics may differ; the observable meaning must not. How content is composed, how state is stored, how a renderer marks its own output, which literal a generated id has, how an adapter anchors its teleported content.
classifications.framework-specific: Historical behaviour of one adapter that the other is not required to reproduce. Narrow, named, and covered by its own test.

notCompared.$comment: Recorded so a reviewer can see what is deliberately outside the comparison, without leaving dead dimensions that look like live protection. Nothing here is a waiver: the extractor never produces these differences in the first place.
notCompared.attributeOrder: Attributes are extracted into a sorted map, so serialisation order cannot produce a difference.
notCompared.rendererMarkers: Vue scope attributes (data-v-*), the Razor ownership marker, the Razor adapter's configuration (data-vf-razor-select-*, including each option's value and the field-control marker on the trigger) and the inert <template data-vf-razor-select="..."> elements holding the options, the chevron and the clear button are dropped by scripts/parity/extract.mjs. What the templates hold is compared the moment the controller renders it.
notCompared.teleportAnchors: Vue's Teleport marks its place in <body> with empty text nodes; the Razor controller appends one empty text node per instance at bootstrap. Neither is an element. That listboxes sit in <body> in instance order is compared through document-order id tokens and the snapshot's bodyListboxes.
notCompared.generatedIdLiterals: Vue's useId writes vf-select-*-v-N and the Razor server writes vf-select-*-r-N; the extractor rewrites every id to its document position, the followed listbox's after the root's, and every aria-controls / aria-labelledby / aria-describedby / for through the same map. A closed select's aria-controls is compared as #dangling.
notCompared.eventTransport: Vue emits update:modelValue; the Razor controller dispatches one bubbling vf-select:value-change with { value }. What is compared is the neutral log each fixture keeps from readiness on, with the instance, as interaction.events - repeats included.
notCompared.styleSerialisation: Both adapters write the listbox's left, top and min-width through the CSSOM at run time. The extractor parses them through the browser and compares the declarations.

platformDivergences.description: Vue: the displayed value, the hidden input and aria-selected are derived from `modelValue` alone - a selection or a clear emits update:modelValue and changes nothing until the parent writes it back. Razor: `model-value` is the initial value only, and the controller applies a selection or a clear itself and dispatches vf-select:value-change.
platformDivergences.reason: A server-rendered select has no parent in the page to emit a request to and wait on. Reproducing the wait would leave every Razor select permanently showing its first value without a script protocol the reference never had. The same divergence as VfDropdown's, VfPopover's and VfGroupBox's.
platformDivergences.comparedAs: Every select scenario of contracts/select/cases.json: the Vue fixtures write update:modelValue back into the prop (v-model), the Razor adapter applies the value directly, and all three targets must land on the same DOM, hidden input, form entries, events, focus and tree - select/interaction-enter-select, select/interaction-option-click and select/interaction-clear among them.
platformDivergences.vueHalfCoveredBy: packages/core/src/components/select/VfSelect.characterization.spec.ts (controlled model: a selection without write-back keeps the old label, hidden value and aria-selected; a clear without write-back keeps the value; forms: a selection not written back keeps the old submitted value)
platformDivergences.razorHalfCoveredBy: packages/razor/tests/Components/SelectComponentTest.php (the server renders the model-value it is given) and scripts/ci/check-razor-browser.mjs (a selection and a clear update the label, the hidden input and FormData, and dispatch one value-change)
platformDivergences.mutationCoveredBy: scripts/baseline/input-mutations.mjs#select-uncontrolled-self-update - the Razor reading applied to the Vue component - is detected by the characterization suite

outsideTheCatalog.$comment: Behaviour that is part of the contract and deliberately not represented as a parity case, each with where it is covered instead.
outsideTheCatalog.teleportToElement: teleportTo given as an HTMLElement is Vue-only; a selector is covered by the Razor browser gate (teleport-to="#razor-overlay-root") and the characterization suite; teleportTo: null is spelled teleport-to="false" by the Razor adapter's null convention.
outsideTheCatalog.reactiveOptions: Options or placeholder changed after render re-derive the label and the listbox in Vue. The Razor options are static server markup; pinned by the characterization suite.
outsideTheCatalog.duplicateValues: Duplicate option values select the first for the label and mark every duplicate aria-selected; Vue warns about the duplicate key. Pinned by the characterization suite and the shared vectors, outside the catalog so no case carries a framework warning.
outsideTheCatalog.outsidePointerdown: The outside close listens for a document click, not pointerdown: a pointerdown or mousedown alone closes nothing. The harness drives whole clicks; the pointerdown half is pinned by the characterization suite and the Razor browser gate.
outsideTheCatalog.focusScopeBranch: Inside an active modal focus trap the open listbox joins the trap's scope. No migrated component owns a trap yet; the branch is pinned by the characterization suite and is outside the Razor controller until a trap exists.
outsideTheCatalog.firstRenderFieldReport: Inside a VfField the Vue select declares floating support during its own setup, after the field rendered, so the field is plain for one tick; the Razor field is floating from the server render. The settled state is compared; the first tick is pinned by the characterization suite.
outsideTheCatalog.tabOutOfTheDocument: Tab from an option of a teleported listbox leaves the document - the listbox is last in <body> - and headless Chrome then delivers junk keydowns to every later scenario on the page. The catalog's Tab scenario renders the listbox in place; the teleported Tab is pinned by the characterization suite and the Razor browser gate.
outsideTheCatalog.disabledClicks: The harness refuses to click a disabled control - a real pointer on a disabled <button> delivers no click, which is the browser's rule, not the component's. A disabled select and a disabled option are compared as static and ownership state (inoperable, excluded from the walk and from the form); that a synthetic click on a disabled option is still refused by the handler is pinned by the characterization suite, and the Razor browser gate clicks a disabled trigger with a real pointer.
outsideTheCatalog.nodeIdentityAcrossOpens: Every open creates a new listbox node on every target. Pinned by the characterization suite and the Razor browser gate.

dom.structure.description: An unexpected element, a missing trigger, hidden input or clear button, a listbox rendered while closed, a listbox left after its leave, a listbox in place where it should be teleported or teleported where it should be in place. The followed listbox is described as its own top-level entry after the root's children. Never approvable.

dom.canonicalClasses.description: vf-* classes on every element: the wrapper and trigger modifiers (size, invalid, open, placeholder, adornments, clear, floating), the listbox's vf-dropdown__menu / vf-select__menu / --top, and the options' selected modifier.

dom.nativeAttributes.description: type, name, value and disabled on the hidden input, the trigger and the options; tabindex (-1 on every option); the listbox's inline position and min-width, compared through the browser's parser.

dom.text.description: Visible text: the displayed label (or placeholder, or nothing under a floating label), each option's label, the field label, description and error.

dom.aria.description: aria-expanded on every trigger, aria-haspopup="listbox", aria-invalid only as "true", role=listbox and role=option, aria-selected on every option, aria-hidden on the adornments and the chevron. No aria-activedescendant anywhere.

dom.productData.description: data-vf-filled on the trigger while the model is non-empty, and a consumer data-testid.

dom.relationships.description: The id graph through document-position tokens, the followed listbox numbered after the root: the trigger's id and aria-controls, the listbox's aria-labelledby, the field label's for and the trigger's aria-describedby.

dom.actionPresence.description: Whether each button is operable: the trigger of a disabled select and a disabled option are inoperable on every target.

dom.wrapperPresence.description: Present so the comparator has a classification for it. A select has no wrapper either adapter may add.

dom.inertAction.description: Present for the same reason. A select renders no inert action.

style.geometry.description: width, height, padding, border width and radius, font size and line height of the wrapper, the trigger, the value, the chevron, the clear button and an in-place listbox.

style.colour.description: colour, background colour and border colour of the same elements.

visual.description: Clipped screenshot of the case root in its initial state, per theme.

visual.postInteraction.description: Clipped screenshot after the interaction, per theme, covering the case root and every listbox it owns wherever it is.

a11y.role.description: Computed role of the trigger (button), the clear button, the listbox and its first, selected and disabled options, read where the listbox is; the aria-hidden chevron is absent.

a11y.name.description: Accessible name of the trigger (its label, or the consumer's aria-label, or the field label), of the clear button, of the listbox (its trigger, through aria-labelledby) and of each read option.

a11y.states.description: focusable, disabled, expanded, hasPopup, invalid and selected as exposed to assistive tech, before and after an interaction.

ownership.controls.description: The component-owned controls: every trigger, the clear button while shown and every option of an open listbox, with tag, role, aria-expanded, aria-haspopup, aria-selected, disabled, tabindex and name; the consumer count beside them and the totals they add up to.

interaction.state.description: The live state after a scenario, per instance: aria-expanded, the trigger's label and classes, the listbox's place, classes, role and options, its geometry and scroll, every listbox in <body> by what names it, the field and a popover around the select, and the transitions.

interaction.events.description: The neutral value log the fixture recorded from readiness on, with the instance and the value. A missing, duplicated or reordered emission differs.

interaction.convergence.description: Whether a closing gesture's DOM equals the target's own render of the closed case it lands on. A leave that left a listbox behind, a stale label or a clear button that did not swap back differs.

interaction.focus.description: Where focus is after the scenario - a trigger, the clear button, an option (by label), another control, the body - and which instance holds it.

interaction.relationships.description: Whether each trigger's aria-controls reaches a listbox labelled by that trigger, on the live DOM, and that nothing carries aria-activedescendant.

interaction.value.description: The hidden input per instance (name, value, disabled, first in the wrapper), the entries of the form around the case and its validity.

interaction.selection.description: Present for the shared comparator. A select carries no caret.

interaction.wrapperPresence.description: Present for the shared comparator. A select renders no wrapper that could appear on one side only.

historicalQuirks.description: ArrowUp opens the select as ArrowDown, Enter and Space do; Home, End and Escape on a closed trigger do nothing and are not prevented.
A keyboard open focuses the selected option counted among the enabled ones, or the first enabled option when the selected one is disabled, missing or absent.
The walk runs over the enabled options only: a disabled option is skipped by the arrows, Home and End, and a click on it does nothing.
Tab is not handled in the listbox: focus moves on and the listbox stays open until an outside click or Escape.
An option click selects without focusing the trigger; a keyboard selection focuses it.
An outside click closes without focusing the trigger - unlike VfDropdown's, which does.
The clear button prevents its mousedown, stops its click, emits '' and focuses the trigger, closing an open listbox.
Escape from an option is handled by the listbox itself and prevented, so the shared stack ignores it; from anywhere else the stack closes the most recently opened select.
The listbox is teleported out of a surrounding popover's panel, so an option click is an outside click to the popover and closes it too.
required, autofocus, form and role reach no element: only aria-*, data-*, title and tabindex are forwarded to the trigger, a string id becomes its id and a string name the hidden input's.
Nothing listens to a form reset: the hidden input's value is its own default, so a reset changes nothing.
An option with value '' is selected by the empty model but does not count as filled: no data-vf-filled, no clear button.
historicalQuirks.reason: Compared as a static case on every target.
